episode.title: Istanbul Put A Roof Over The Bosphorus

synopsis: The Bosphorus is spanned by a vast glass canopy and Hagia Sophia stands beneath it, with lit ferry docks and covered markets running underneath.
caption:
Istanbul, 2512. The strait was roofed over, end to end, to hold the weather out.

The city stayed. People built the market back underneath the glass, on the same quays their families had always used.

Figs and lemons grow in the warm air under the roof. The ferries still run, on the same routes, in permanent shelter. At dusk the lamps come on and the whole strait glows from inside.

A fictional future, created with AI.

Would you take the ferry or walk the covered quay?
music: A single sustained sub-bass drone at one steady level for the whole duration, built from deep low-frequency air and distant structural resonance. It holds the same volume from the first second to the last, stays free of percussion, rhythm, melody, vocals and high frequencies, and ends mid-tone so the loop is seamless.

shots.prompt:
Shot 1, exactly 4 seconds at 24 fps: a wide god's-eye view from high aerial or near-orbital height. The very first frame already contains BOTH the real city's recognisable landmark or skyline AND the full extent of what was built to keep it liveable. One slow, single-direction camera move only (a descent or a forward glide); no pan, orbit, whip or cut inside the shot. No setup, no approach, no delayed reveal: what the episode is about is legible in frame one.

The whole Bosphorus fills frame one beneath a fixed near-orbital camera, spanned end to end by an immense glazed canopy whose steel ribs catch low sun. Hagia Sophia and the Blue Mosque read clearly through the glass on the European shore, their domes and minarets intact and darkened with age. Ferry wakes trace pale lines on the sheltered water below the roof, and the Golden Horn curves away under a continuous lit ceiling. The camera descends slowly and straight down through the four seconds, holding the same heading and focal length, so the canopy ribs widen steadily across the frame and the two domes grow larger at the centre. Warm interior light glows up through the glass from the covered city beneath.

Shot 2, exactly 4 seconds at 24 fps: a low, human-scale view of the SAME place after a hard cut, from a completely different vantage point. People are visible and going about ordinary daily life: walking, trading, carrying, eating, queueing. Warm practical light from windows, stalls and signage fills the frame. The same recognisable landmark stays readable somewhere in the background or on the horizon so the two shots read as one city. One slow, single-direction camera move only.

A low view along a covered quay directly beneath the canopy, the glazed roof arching overhead and Hagia Sophia's dome filling the background through the glass. Market stalls line the quay with hanging lamps, stacked fruit, copper pots and bolts of cloth, and a dense crowd moves along the waterfront carrying bags and crates. A ferry is tied at the dock and passengers step across the gangway. Warm stall light and the cool daylight through the roof mix on wet stone. The camera glides forward slowly and steadily along the quay for the full duration at a constant height.
